subject: Dedicated capacity: pool composition, TPS split, and GPU preference
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Toma <alex.toma@quantifyai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: pool composition, TPS split, and GPU preference — post-call recap

Alex — thanks for the time this morning. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the technical workshop. I’ve attached the token profile CSV you shared and our internal GPU tradeoff brief for context.

Recap of your deployment needs (as stated on call):
- Deployment mode leaning: Dedicated capacity (customer-managed VPC as possibility once security review completes)
- Target sustained TPS: 45 requests/sec (inference calls)
- Burst window: up to ~120 TPS for 5–12 minute spikes (batch processing + user surge)
- Average token lengths: 60% classification/short prompts (~40–120 tokens), 40% long-form generation (avg ~450 tokens)
- Latency SLO target: 95th <= 220ms for short prompts; long-gen tolerates higher p95 (~1.2s)
- Security: QuantifyAI likely needs HSM/KMS with FIPS controls if moving to VPC/private deployment

Questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Preferred GPU flavors — you mentioned A100-80GB for quality, but also asked about H100 for pure throughput. We
   want to confirm model family (gpt-3.5-like vs Llama 3 70B) and whether FP16/4-bit quantization is acceptable.
2) Concurrency shape — are requests coming as steady single-user streams or as short parallel bursts (many small calls)?
3) Cold-start tolerance — any strict constraints around warm-up windows during autoscale?

Proposed short sizing hypothesis (initial):
- Steady pool: 3 x A100-80GB (handles avg 45 TPS with KV cache for short prompts and stable p95)
- Burst pool (autoscale): up to +6 GPUs (mix of A100 + H100 depending on final model choice) to hit 120 TPS peaks
- Autoscale policy: fast scale-up (30–60s) for burst; conservative scale-down (10–15m) to avoid flapping
- Caching: prefix KV caching for short prompts to reduce token compute for the 60% short-request mix

Next steps:
- Karthik: please validate the sizing hypothesis against model family and token shape (see attached token CSV).
- Alex: confirm model variant and whether quantization is acceptable by EOD Thu. Also confirm key management constraints (HSM/FIPS).
- I’ll schedule a 60–90 minute tech workshop next week between QuantifyAI infra and our SEs to validate network/VPC requirements and run a quick perf benchmark plan.

Attachments: quantify_token_profile.csv (token mix), gpu_sku_tradeoffs.pdf (internal brief)

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: pool composition, TPS split, and GPU preference — post-call recap

Thanks for the clear recap, Irene — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Model family: we plan to run a mix — production-quality Llama 3 70B for customer-facing assistants (long-gen) and a tuned 13B for short classification/embeddings. We are open to quantization on the 13B, but Llama 3 70B must stay high fidelity (no heavy quantization).
- KMS/HSM: if we go VPC/private, we require HSM-backed key wrapping and FIPS 140-2 controls. Hosted API would be easier but procurement is pushing for a private option.
- Concurrency: most traffic is concurrent small calls (webhooks + UI lookups) during business hours, plus scheduled batch jobs at night that trigger short burst windows. So both steady concurrency and short spikes matter.
- Cold start: we can tolerate a 1–2s cold-start for long-gen, but short prompts must be highly available — long warm-up is not acceptable.

One more ask: can you provide a quick example cost delta (ballpark monthly cost) between A100-only vs mixed A100/H100 pool given the sizing hypothesis? That will help accelerate procurement.

—Alex
Alex Toma
Head of ML Ops, QuantifyAI
alex.toma@quantifyai.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alex Toma <alex.toma@quantifyai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: pool composition, TPS split, and GPU preference — sizing notes

Alex — thanks for the extra detail. Quick technical notes and a refined sizing estimate based on the model split you gave: 

Assumptions used:
- Llama 3 70B at FP16 (no aggressive quantization), long-gen average 450 tokens per request
- 13B quantized to 4-bit for classification/short prompts (avg 80 tokens)
- Short prompts are highly latency-sensitive; long-gen less so

Sizing suggestions (refined):
1) Steady pool (latency-sensitive short calls + baseline long-gen):
   - 2 x A100-80GB (primary for Llama 70B inference shards)
   - 2 x A40/A100-40GB or 2 x H100-80GB (for quantized 13B; H100 improves throughput but at higher cost)
   - This gives headroom for sustained 45 TPS with p95 headroom for short prompts using KV cache and batching where appropriate.
2) Burst pool: +4 GPUs (mix of H100 and A100) to hit 120 TPS peaks — recommend pre-warmed burst nodes (warm pool) to avoid cold-start penalties for short prompts
3) Autoscale behavior: fast spin-up but rely on warm pool for critical short-prompt SLAs. Use request-priority routing: prioritize short prompts through a low-latency pool, route long-gen to burst/scale-up nodes.

Cost delta (ballpark monthly, USD):
- A100-heavy (steady+burst as A100): ~$65k–85k/month (depends on instance pricing and reserved commit)
- Mixed H100+A100: ~$90k–120k/month (H100 premium covers throughput improvement on quantized model)

I’ve put the detailed calc into the shared drive link (see related links). If QuantifyAI wants a tighter number, we can run a quick perf benchmark (30–60 minutes) using a representative prompt set and produce an updated projection.

Action items for workshop:
- Confirm final model binaries and allowed quantization levels (QuantifyAI)
- Workshop agenda: network/VPC firewall rules, KMS/HSM integration pattern, benchmark plan, and draft autoscale policy

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — planning notes and concrete next steps: 

1) Technical workshop: Tue 2026-07-28 @ 10:00 PT — invite will go to Alex’s infra and QuantifyAI security. Karthik and Soojin will run the perf/benchmark availability and network checklist.
2) Deliverables prior to workshop (QuantifyAI): final model binaries (or container images), confirmation on quantization policy per model, and HSM/KMS requirements doc.
3) Deliverables prior to workshop (Redwood): updated cost delta table (A100 vs mixed) and a short perf-run plan (30–60 min) that Karthik will execute with QuantifyAI during workshop.
4) Procurement ask: Marissa — please prepare a draft reserved commitment worksheet (12-mo and 36-mo) using the A100-heavy and mixed-H100 proposals so Alex’s procurement team has ballpark numbers.

I’ve attached the token profile and internal GPU brief again. If QuantifyAI confirms the model set and quantization policy by Thu EOD, we’ll lock in the workshop and the perf plan.

Best,
Irene
